# 華嚴五教止觀

**ID:** T1867
**Volume:** T45
**Category:** 華嚴部類
**Original Category:** 諸宗部
**Byline:** 隋 杜順說
**Dynasty:** 隋
**Date:** 557–640
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1867

## Contributors
- 法順 (A000525)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Huáyán wǔ jiào zhǐ guān* is the founding doctrinal text traditionally attributed to [杜順](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%A0%86) Dùshùn (557–640), the *first patriarch* of the Chinese Huáyán school. In 1 fascicle, it presents the doctrine of *zhǐguān* (止觀, śamatha-vipaśyanā / cessation-and-insight) as it is configured for each of the *Five Teachings* (五教) — the doxographical hierarchy that [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) Fǎzàng would later canonise in his *[Wǔ jiào zhāng 五教章](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074)*. The work thus stands as the early outline of Huáyán doxographical structure that Fǎzàng would systematise some decades later.

**Abstract**

The bracket adopted here (580 – 640) reflects [杜順](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%A0%86) Dùshùn's mature life. The traditional ascription to Dùshùn is sometimes questioned by modern scholarship (Gimello 1976; Hamar 2007), which has noted that the doctrinal apparatus — particularly the *Five Teachings* schema — appears more Táng-period than late-Suí. The Five-Teachings doxography in its mature form is canonically associated with Fǎzàng (cf. [T1866](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074)), and the present work's relation to Fǎzàng's later, more systematic articulation is debated. One plausible reading is that the present text preserves Dùshùn's *embryonic* sketch of a doxographical schema that his disciples ([智儼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%84%BC) Zhìyǎn, then Fǎzàng) would later develop and canonise. The traditional attribution — accepted by [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) Zōngmì and the later Huáyán-school tradition — remains the working assumption in most secondary scholarship.

The work is preserved in the Taishō (T1867) on the Korean *Tripiṭaka Koreana* and *yuán* 原 (original-block) witnesses.
